## Conflicts noticed

Seen by the shard readers and recorded here unresolved. "c:N" is forum comment N; "d:N" is discussion N. Several pairs are the same author at different dates.

- **Atomicity and "one thought".** Christian: limit a unit to one thought ([d2646](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/2646)) and each note gets a single concern ([c16133](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16133#Comment_16133)). Sascha: one statement per Zettel is inappropriate ([c4833](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4833#Comment_4833)), "no one knows what a single thought is" ([c18464](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/18464#Comment_18464)) against capturing a thought "with some confidence that I can capture it all" ([c17826](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/17826#Comment_17826)). Sascha: improving the idea is improving the note, one idea per note ([c26101](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/26101#Comment_26101)), while his own archive holds notes "on all levels of atomicity" ([c25136](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25136#Comment_25136)). Sascha set strict atomicity aside for a book project ([c22248](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/22248#Comment_22248)) and said one note or several "does not matter in general" ([c13402](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/13402#Comment_13402)). Christian: Gemmell's "Atomic Thoughts" summarizes atomicity well ([d2468](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/2468)). Sascha: that essay "doesn't paint the whole picture" ([c17119](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/17119#Comment_17119)).
- **Length.** Sascha: shorter is not atomic, and an atomic note can run to thousands of words ([c16860](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16860#Comment_16860), [c26716](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/26716#Comment_26716)). Christian: separating observation from interpretation keeps notes concise ([c11833](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/11833#Comment_11833)). Sascha: super-short claim notes "work very well" ([c23721](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/23721#Comment_23721)) against recommending full notes over Luhmann's super-short ones ([c24234](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/24234#Comment_24234)).
- **Finished vs. unfinished notes.** Sascha 2019-2020: notes are self-contained, "no half-assed notes" ([c2160](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/2160#Comment_2160)), written right in one session ([c4544](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4544#Comment_4544), [c4630](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4630#Comment_4630)). Sascha 2025-2026: proto-atomic notes are "completely fine" ([c25019](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25019#Comment_25019)), you will have many unfinished non-atomic notes ([c24666](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/24666#Comment_24666)), and parts of his archive are messy ([c25707](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25707#Comment_25707)).
- **Splitting notes.** Christian: extract parts once a note proves divisible, and where to cut is mostly gut feeling ([c19866](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/19866#Comment_19866)). Sascha: "no benefit yet in just separating" sub-points ([c21307](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21307#Comment_21307)), and mapping each note to one claim limits flexibility ([c12946](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/12946#Comment_12946)).
- **Titles.** Sascha: put the note's claim in the title ([c16820](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16820#Comment_16820)), yet he does not follow the claim-as-title convention ([c16815](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16815#Comment_16815)).
- **Link context.** Sascha: every link gets an explicit reason ([c5038](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/5038#Comment_5038)). Christian: a plain link inside a sentence is enough, and an unlinked note found by search is acceptable ([c13494](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/13494#Comment_13494), [c5010](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/5010#Comment_5010)). Weak.
- **Whether links are required.** Sascha: direct links give the archive life, and you should never create unlinked notes ([c4817](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4817#Comment_4817), [c5965](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/5965#Comment_5965), [c7683](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/7683#Comment_7683)). Christian: "There's no Zettel police enforcing links", and an overview can stand in ([c16073](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16073#Comment_16073)).
- **Tags.** Sascha: tags don't scale, don't rely on them ([c1553](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/1553#Comment_1553)), and tags get worse with use while structure notes get better ([c4882](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4882#Comment_4882)). Christian: tagging fits thinking in subjects ([c1547](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/1547#Comment_1547)), tags help narrow down ([c25766](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25766#Comment_25766)), and links beat tags long-term but tags should not be thrown out ([c4509](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4509#Comment_4509)). Christian also asks whether tags and links really differ at some level ([c22610](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/22610#Comment_22610)).
- **Structure-note form.** Sascha: simple lists have no more structural value than tags, so nest or use tables ([c7624](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/7624#Comment_7624)), and presenting the table-of-contents style as the main form was a mistake ([c9409](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/9409#Comment_9409)). Christian: his structure notes are mostly bullet lists, one link per bullet plus a sentence of context ([c7623](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/7623#Comment_7623)).
- **When to add structure.** Sascha: start structure notes from the beginning ([c15389](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/15389#Comment_15389)), and he does no recurring maintenance on his structure notes ([c19085](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/19085#Comment_19085)). Christian: when to introduce structure is central to longevity ([c12470](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/12470#Comment_12470)), he starts from a larger "molecule" ([c23240](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/23240#Comment_23240)), and he cleans up a note only when he runs into it ([c13934](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/13934#Comment_13934)). Sascha: a properly organized archive cannot get cluttered ([c1361](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/1361#Comment_1361)) against complexity outgrowing the user turning it into "a mess" ([c22113](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/22113#Comment_22113)).
- **Folgezettel.** Sascha: structure notes are simply better ([d2470](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/2470)), Folgezettel are "obsolete and outdated... a distraction" ([c23412](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/23412#Comment_23412)), and he ditched them ([c24851](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/24851#Comment_24851)). Sascha also: they are not mutually exclusive with structure notes ([c17179](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/17179#Comment_17179)), "Folgezettel don't harm" ([c23721](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/23721#Comment_23721)), they are fine as a pre-staging phase ([c24471](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/24471#Comment_24471)), and you should pick one because both add load ([c21748](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21748#Comment_21748)). Christian: looking for a context first is "a must" with Folgezettel ([c21017](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21017#Comment_21017)). Sascha: a "weak must" ([c21020](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21020#Comment_21020)).
- **Paragraph-level IDs.** Sascha: give part of a note an ID and link to it ([c6950](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/6950#Comment_6950)) against calling paragraph-level linking a methodological mistake ([c8233](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8233#Comment_8233)), later abandoned ([c8823](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8823#Comment_8823)).
- **Literature notes and note types.** Sascha: no difference between literature notes and his own ideas ([c8656](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8656#Comment_8656), [c10491](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/10491#Comment_10491)), "I don't do literature notes" ([c3839](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/3839#Comment_3839)), the distinction makes no sense ([c12625](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/12625#Comment_12625), [c25584](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25584#Comment_25584)), and typology brings no benefit ([c18586](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/18586#Comment_18586), [c11563](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/11563#Comment_11563)). Sascha also allows excerpts in the archive ([c14880](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/14880#Comment_14880)), says notes made outside need only a source reference ([c13285](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/13285#Comment_13285)), and says a note about a book is not a literature note ([c16852](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16852#Comment_16852)). Christian: discards reading scribbles after processing ([c10488](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/10488#Comment_10488)), treats a mostly-quote note as a reference note that later gets absorbed ([c21746](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21746#Comment_21746), [c21077](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21077#Comment_21077)), and keeps the structure/content distinction ([c9016](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/9016#Comment_9016)).
- **Sources.** Sascha: the reference only honors the author ([c8772](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8772#Comment_8772)), and divorcing a quote from its source is acceptable when the aim is knowledge ([c14645](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/14645#Comment_14645)). Sascha also: anchor citations carefully, check the primary source, and reference faithfully ([c12345](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/12345#Comment_12345), [c12372](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/12372#Comment_12372), [c8852](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8852#Comment_8852), [c16697](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16697#Comment_16697)). Sascha does not store sources unless he returns to them often ([c17803](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/17803#Comment_17803)). Christian keeps PDFs named by citekey ([c8148](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8148#Comment_8148)). Sascha: process a text once and never touch it again ([c1928](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/1928#Comment_1928)), but he reads books twice ([c2367](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/2367#Comment_2367)).
- **Inbox and fleeting notes.** Sascha: no inbox, file directly, no fleeting notes ([c4543](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/4543#Comment_4543), [c10373](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/10373#Comment_10373), [c11984](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/11984#Comment_11984), [c15123](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/15123#Comment_15123)), and getting rid of the inbox marks system quality ([c16420](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16420#Comment_16420)). Sascha also: world, then inbox, then Zettelkasten ([c2350](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/2350#Comment_2350), [c7885](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/7885#Comment_7885)), he reintroduced an inbox ([c16996](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/16996#Comment_16996)), and an empty inbox is almost the opposite of good practice ([c22072](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/22072#Comment_22072)). Christian: keeps work in progress and a daily capture note outside the archive ([c10604](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/10604#Comment_10604), [c20096](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/20096#Comment_20096)) and suggests a #fleeting tag ([c6049](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/6049#Comment_6049)).
- **Review.** Sascha: a regular review habit is very beneficial ([c18333](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/18333#Comment_18333)) against spending zero time reviewing ([c20847](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/20847#Comment_20847)).
- **What belongs in the archive.** Sascha: everything that counts as information, including journal and workout entries ([c3141](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/3141#Comment_3141), [c5128](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/5128#Comment_5128), [c17796](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/17796#Comment_17796), [c7159](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/7159#Comment_7159)), anything useful ([c8320](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/8320#Comment_8320)), spreadsheets and experiment data ([c9646](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/9646#Comment_9646), [c9664](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/9664#Comment_9664)), and plenty of todos ([c25504](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25504#Comment_25504)). Sascha also: an archive free of TODOs is not polluted ([c10990](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/10990#Comment_10990)), only material he starts thinking about enters ([c25586](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25586#Comment_25586)), and non-book input goes to a "2nd brain" ([c19409](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/19409#Comment_19409)). Christian: no ongoing diary ([c3122](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/3122#Comment_3122), [c226](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/226#Comment_226)), some things don't belong ([c9984](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/9984#Comment_9984)), tasks are noise ([c25487](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25487#Comment_25487)), and experimental data stays external ([c25144](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/25144#Comment_25144)), yet "if stuff's outside of the ZK, it might was well not exist" ([c23070](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/23070#Comment_23070)).
- **One archive or several.** Sascha: multiple archives are unnecessary ([c20297](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/20297#Comment_20297)). Christian: two folders can be easier than one untangled by tags ([c20304](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/20304#Comment_20304)).
- **Versioning.** Christian: no value in versioning ([c20781](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/20781#Comment_20781)) against keeping versioned how-to notes with the old ID as a hub ([c21517](https://forum.zettelkasten.de/discussion/comment/21517#Comment_21517)).

## Coverage log

Method: `GET https://forum.zettelkasten.de/api/v2/discussions?insertUserID=<id>&limit=100&page=<n>` and `GET .../api/v2/comments?insertUserID=<id>&limit=100&page=<n>`, paged until no `rel="next"` link, 1.5 s between requests, anonymous. The API returns each post's full HTML body; quoted text from other users (`<blockquote>`) was set aside so only the staff member's own words were read. ## Known gaps

- **Posts hidden from anonymous readers.** The API filters rows after paging: page 1 of `comments?insertUserID=4&limit=100` returned 93 rows, not 100. This is consistent with posts in categories closed to anonymous users (members-only or staff areas). That cause is inferred, not confirmed. Their number and content cannot be checked without a forum account. All counts here cover only the anonymously visible posts.
- **Profile activity pages need sign-in.** `https://forum.zettelkasten.de/profile/<name>` redirects to `/entry/signin`, so the per-profile post counts the forum keeps could not be compared against the API totals.
- **Thread context.** Only the staff members' own words were read. Other users' posts, and text the staff quoted from others, were not read. A claim's scope (for example, a reply that answers one user's specific setup) may be narrower than the claim text suggests; the permalink gives the full context.
- **Edited posts.** The API returns the current body. Earlier versions of edited posts are not visible.
- **Images and attachments.** Screenshots and attached images of example zettels were not read; only the post text was.
- **Other staff.** Only the two blog authors listed at https://zettelkasten.de/authors/ count as staff here. Forum moderators who are not blog authors, and guest blog authors, are out of scope.
- **Coverage is logged per thread, not per post.** The 5,563 staff posts (301 discussions started, 5,262 comments) fall in 2,225 threads. Each thread row covers all staff posts in it. Claim rows link the individual comment permalinks.
- **Extraction was split across twelve parallel readers.** Each `read-no-claims` judgment was made by one reader and not double-checked. Every quote was checked by script against the post it cites, and a random sample of 30 was re-fetched live and matched.
